text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (11.7% of 1,337, expected 3.2%, score 5.93, z 1.01, 18 documented, 3 documented 99215s, 15 notes with 0 lacking labs). The summary is cautious, 'inconclusive' is reasonable, and it names symptom-only and Z09 claims correctly. However, it has a few misstatements and internal tensions, and the next steps are generic and omit the specific recommendation in the text. An investigator would need to redo some analysis.","problems":["Claims the elevated 99215 share 'appears in every complexity tier', which is true by the card's rows (all tiers exceed the all-provider share), but it presents this without numbers and 4-tier rows show only modest excess (0.188 vs 0.136).","States 'the panel is also skewed toward 99214' without any panel-level evidence on the card, other than the mix (816 of 1,337 are 99214); this is vague and unsupported as a contrast.","The '14% for the comparison providers' figure does not match the card: the all-provider rate for 99215 is 0.136 (about 14%), which is for 'below_billed', so it is fine, but the 1.3% documentation share is not stated as a key limitation.","Internally contradictory framing: calls the low-complexity pattern 'consistent with upcoding' and then says the charts 'do not point toward upcoding' while the leaning is inconclusive; the investigator gets mixed signals.","The 37% low-complexity share uses 0 or 1 conditions, while the card's 0.369 is of 99215s; fine, but the z-score of 1.01 is not interpreted, so it is unclear that it is not notable versus peers.","The listed next steps are generic ('larger sample', 'Re-screen') and omit the specific, better action in the text (request charts for the cited low-complexity 99215 claims); the example claims in the fixed list include a 99214 and lack the Z09 and symptom-only cases.","Describing 0 of 15 as 'no notes claiming substantial data review lacked a lab line' is confusing wording; the 'no numbers matched: 99215' flag is just a CPT code, so it is harmless."]}
